summary.title: Programming Projects for Advanced Beginners #1: ASCII art
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a program that converts an image into ASCII art by loading pixels, converting them to brightness values, and mapping brightness to characters printed in the terminal.
takeaways: Load an image with an image processing library and read its pixel dimensions.
Store RGB pixel tuples in a 2-dimensional array and iterate over it by x and y.
Convert RGB values to a single brightness value using average, lightness, or luminosity formulas.
Map brightness values (0-255) onto a character ramp, then print the result, stretching characters horizontally and resizing the image to fit the terminal.
summary.summary: This is a guided programming project for advanced beginners that builds an image-to-ASCII-art converter. It is split into five steps: loading an image, building a 2D pixel matrix, converting RGB to brightness, mapping brightness to a character ramp, and printing to the terminal, with intermediate output to check at each stage. The page suggests libraries per language (Pillow for Python, MiniMagick for Ruby, CamanJS for JavaScript) and offers extension ideas such as Matrix-green colouring, alternative brightness mappings, inverting brightness, webcam input, and colour output. The author provides a Python example solution as a reference.
